newsitem.title: USA: Investigator says did not fake McVeigh confession.
newsitem.headline: Investigator says did not fake McVeigh confession.

text.p: A private investigator who was accused of concocting a confession of Oklahoma City bombing suspect Timothy McVeigh said he did not do it and has resigned from McVeigh's defence team, a newspaper reported on Thursday.

The investigator, Richard Reyna from the Houston suburb of Conroe, told the Houston Chronicle he quit because he was angry with McVeigh attorney Stephen Jones for not squelching the rumours that he had written a fake confession that Jones said was the basis for recent news reports saying McVeigh had admitted his guilt.
"Stephen Jones said he was going to take care of this, and as far as I'm concerned, he didn't," Reyna said. "It looks like I turned on Timothy McVeigh and that's damaging to my livelihood."

Jones' claimed that recent reports in the Dallas Morning News and Playboy magazine, saying McVeigh admitted planting the April 19, 1995 bomb, were based on false defence documents. Jones said the documents were concocted as part of an elaborate scheme to flush out another suspect.

An Oklahoma free-lance writer, J.D. Cash, who has followed the case, said Reyna had written the fake confession, but Reyna said that was not true. "It's an absolute falsehood. I never falsified any documents."
Reyna said he interviewed McVeigh extensively, but would not comment on what the suspect told him.
"I put what (McVeigh) told me in report forms and gave those reports to Stephen Jones. I've never given those reports to anybody but Stephen Jones," Reyna said.
Reyna, whom Jones hired in May 1995 to work on the case, said he resigned from the McVeigh team on Wednesday.
McVeigh goes on trial in Denver, Colo. starting March 31. He is accused of planting the truck bomb that killed 168 people and injured 500 others in downtown Oklahoma City.
